prompt: The developer asks to merge their branch, and the change shows up for the team to discuss.
why: Asking to merge a branch puts the change where the team can see it, discuss it and approve it. That request is a pull request.
trap: The review happens on it; opening it is the PR.

prompt: A page on GitHub shows the diff, a description and a test plan.
tells: A page on GitHub shows the diff
why: The diff, description and test plan on one page are a pull request, where the change is reviewed before merging.
trap: Reviewers use it, but the page is the PR.

prompt: Instead of pushing straight to main, she opens a request to bring her changes in.
tells: opens a request to bring her changes in
why: Instead of pushing straight to main, the change goes in through a request others can review. That's a pull request.
trap: The branch already exists; the request is new.

prompt: The description explains what changed, why, and how it was tested.
tells: explains what changed, why, and how it was tested
why: Saying what changed, why, and how it was tested helps reviewers understand the pull request quickly.
trap: A commit message is shorter and per change.

prompt: A draft request is opened early to get feedback on the direction.
tells: A draft request is opened early
why: A draft pull request asks for early feedback on direction before the work is finished.
trap: Feedback comes in review, but the move is opening a draft PR.

prompt: CI results and reviewer comments all appear on the proposed change before it merges.
tells: on the proposed change before it merges
why: The pull request collects the diff, CI results and review comments in one place before the change merges.
trap: CI and review are parts of it; the container is the PR.
